# Practical Trade-offs Between Vector Databases and Traditional Search Engines for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

## Summary

Vector databases provide high throughput and low latency for similarity search operations, which is critical for real-time AI applications. [S2] Vector databases require robust data ingestion pipelines and embedding models, which add infrastructure overhead and preprocessing complexity. [S2] Vector databases have more severe security and privacy implications than traditional search engines when processing sensitive information for RAG applications. [S1] Vector databases become most favorable for RAG applications with minimum data requirements of 100+ documents to effectively capture semantic relationships. [S2]

## Key findings

- Vector databases provide high throughput and low latency for similarity search operations, which is critical for real-time AI applications. [S2]
- Vector databases require robust data ingestion pipelines and embedding models, which add infrastructure overhead and preprocessing complexity. [S2]
- Vector databases have more severe security and privacy implications than traditional search engines when processing sensitive information for RAG applications. [S1]
- Vector databases support enterprise-grade security features including role-based access control (RBAC) and encryption, which meet security standards for sensitive information. [S2]

Vector databases have more severe security and privacy implications than traditional search engines when processing sensitive information for RAG applications. [S1]

Vector databases support enterprise-grade security features including role-based access control (RBAC) and encryption, which meet security standards for sensitive information. [S2]

## Failure Modes and Resilience

High-frequency updates can challenge vector indexes, which often need to be rebuilt or optimized to incorporate new data. [S2]

The trade-off between vector databases and traditional search engines becomes most favorable for use cases requiring real-time up-to-date information retrieval. [S1]
